bridges.statement: Human persons are immaterial substantial entities—souls—that contain consciousness and animate their bodies.
Conscious mental states have properties that physical brain states lack, so consciousness is neither identical with nor reducible to the brain.
The unity, indivisibility, and persistence of persons through physical change require a substantial soul.
Free agency, rational inference, and mental causation require a nonphysical subject rather than an exclusively physical causal chain.
Brain–mind dependence and correlation do not establish mind–brain identity and are compatible with an embodied soul using the brain.
Empirical and experiential evidence, including some near-death reports, can support a cumulative case without being the primary philosophical demonstration.
No coherent, evidenced soul is needed to explain life, consciousness, cognition, or personal characteristics.
Systematic alteration of thought, memory, personality, and awareness by physical conditions supports bodily production of mind and conflicts with an independently functioning soul.
Conscious capacities occur by degrees across biological systems and emerge through continuous physical organization rather than an added immaterial entity.
A soul that interacts with bodies would have observable consequences, yet controlled inquiry has not verified such an entity.
Near-death, out-of-body, and paranormal reports are inconsistent, culturally conditioned, reproducible through brain stimulation, or otherwise insufficient evidence.
The proponent must positively define and demonstrate the proposed additional immaterial component rather than infer it merely from gaps in physical explanation.

sections.title: definition, scientific reach, and burden of proof
intentionality, truth-bearing thought, and subjective experience
unity, indivisibility, and identity through change
free will, rational inference, and mental causation
brain dependence, embodiment, animals, and emergence
empirical testing, near-death experiences, and paranormal claims

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the debate is not a scientific question
science by definition is a discipline
virtually nothing to say about the non-physical
moves.attributionBasis: Hernandez's uninterrupted affirmative opening after the moderator's explicit handoff.
moves.proposition: Because the proposed soul is nonphysical while science studies the physical, the motion is fundamentally metaphysical rather than directly decidable by science.
moves.inventoryRationale: Establishes Hernandez's method and limits the kind of evidence he says the motion requires.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there is no piece of empirical data
our conclusions that we draw from the data
questions about metaphysics not science
moves.attributionBasis: Clear continuation of Hernandez's opening.
moves.proposition: The rival views can accept the same empirical observations while drawing different philosophical conclusions, so empirical equivalence does not settle the ontology of consciousness.
moves.inventoryRationale: Clarifies that Hernandez does not deny empirical facts but disputes their metaphysical interpretation.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: consciousness is not physical
I am more than a brain body
the soul is an immaterial substance
moves.attributionBasis: Clear affirmative opening with an explicit statement of the case and definition.
moves.proposition: A soul is an immaterial substance that contains consciousness and animates the body; Hernandez's case is that consciousness is nonphysical and the person is more than brain and body.
moves.inventoryRationale: Supplies the operative definition and the two principal affirmative burdens.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the mind and brain are not identical
my thoughts or beliefs can be true or false
no state of my brain is true or false
moves.attributionBasis: Uninterrupted affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Thoughts and beliefs can be true or false, whereas brain states and functions are not truth-bearers; therefore mind and brain have different properties and are not identical.
moves.inventoryRationale: Core property-dualism inference using the stated identity principle.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: consciousness is a first-person private access kind of thing
mental states have intentionality
when I'm hungry my neurons aren't hungry
moves.attributionBasis: Uninterrupted affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Conscious states are privately accessible, qualitative, and intentional in ways publicly observable brain states are not, indicating a difference in kind rather than mere physical description.
moves.inventoryRationale: Combines closely connected first-person-access and intentionality distinctions without crossing speakers.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: difference between a cause or dependence relationship
cause or effect does not establish identity
it doesn't follow that he is a guitar
moves.attributionBasis: Uninterrupted affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Hernandez concedes that brain alterations affect mental states but argues that causal dependence does not entail identity, as damage to an instrument can impair music without identifying musician, music, and instrument.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important explicit concession and the principal answer to dependence evidence.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: messing with states of my brain
it doesn't follow that they're the same thing
he's going to have to show identity
moves.attributionBasis: Uninterrupted affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Even expected mind–brain dependence cannot establish physicalism unless every property of mind and brain is shown to match in both directions.
moves.inventoryRationale: States Hernandez's demanded inference from correlation to identity more precisely than the analogy alone.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: purely physical objects can be divided
I cannot be divided
therefore I am a soul
moves.attributionBasis: Clear affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Physical aggregates admit division by degrees, but a person is an all-or-nothing subject; therefore a person is not merely a physical aggregate but a soul.
moves.inventoryRationale: The concise formal statement of the indivisibility argument.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: aggregates do not retain identity change
I do maintain identity to change
therefore I am a soul
moves.attributionBasis: Clear affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Unlike changing physical aggregates, the person persists as the same subject through change; therefore personal identity is grounded in an immaterial soul.
moves.inventoryRationale: Formal statement of the persistence argument, distinct from indivisibility.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: argument from free will
originator or source of your will
every physical event must necessarily have a prior physical cause
moves.attributionBasis: Clear affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: Free will requires the agent to originate action, whereas physical causal closure makes every bodily event the product of a prior physical cause; a nonphysical agent is therefore required.
moves.inventoryRationale: Introduces the affirmative's central agency argument and its definition of free will.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: came to be an atheist based on intellectual reasons
posit something like a soul
you give up intellectual integrity and moral responsibility
moves.attributionBasis: Clear affirmative opening.
moves.proposition: If beliefs are rationally adopted and persons are morally accountable, agents must possess the freedom supplied by something like a soul rather than being wholly determined physical systems.
moves.inventoryRationale: Connects free agency to rational and moral responsibility, a recurring later dispute.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: only talking about scientific evidence
we don't have empirical verifiable facts
being unexplained is not an explanation
moves.attributionBasis: Aron Ra's negative opening follows the moderator's explicit handoff.

responseComponents.component: Rejects excluding science: without empirical verification, an interacting soul claim lacks evidential content.
Denies that unexplained observations can serve as a philosophical explanation or favor the soul.

moves.proposition: Scientific evidence is the intelligible evidential standard for an allegedly real soul, and unexplained phenomena neither verify nor explain one.
moves.inventoryRationale: Directly contests Hernandez's attempt to place the soul beyond scientific adjudication.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: an invisible spiritual version of ourselves
there would be a way for science to determine that
possess someone else's body
moves.attributionBasis: Clear continuation of Aron Ra's opening.

responseComponents.component: Argues that even a supernatural soul would be scientifically detectable if it controlled, left, or entered physical bodies.
Tests the definition's claim that a soul animates a body by asking what observable control or separability would follow.

moves.proposition: If a separate soul inhabits and operates the body, its control, departure, or transfer should produce effects that science could detect even if the entity itself were supernatural.
moves.inventoryRationale: Converts the definition into empirical expectations rather than treating nonphysicality as immunity from inquiry.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the theory of vitalism was disproved
there is no life force animating our bodies
never need for such a thing
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.
moves.proposition: Modern biology explains living bodies without the once-proposed animating life force, removing a traditional explanatory role for a soul.
moves.inventoryRationale: Addresses the soul's alleged animating function through biological sufficiency.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: consciousness is just an awareness of self
simple animals with no brain at all
greater awareness and higher consciousness
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.
moves.proposition: Consciousness is graded awareness and environmental perception found even in simple organisms without brains; additional sensory and neural organization yields higher degrees rather than introducing a soul.
moves.inventoryRationale: Foundational evolutionary-continuity and emergence argument.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: how did your supernatural immortal soul lose
change our personalities
drugs and surgery and other physical trauma
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.

responseComponents.component: Argues that the breadth of impairment—thought and personality, not merely output—does not resemble damage to an external instrument.
Presents systematic physical alteration of the person as evidence for bodily mind production, while phrasing it as evidence rather than a formal identity proof.

moves.proposition: Brain damage, drugs, and surgery can alter reasoning, feeling, personality, and proclivities, which supports bodily dependence of the self and conflicts with an independently competent spiritual passenger.
moves.inventoryRationale: Principal negative dependence argument; it is preserved as evidential support rather than a deductive disproof.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: people professing to have had these experiences
no consistency between their accounts
if it were really real
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.
moves.proposition: Professed out-of-body experiences lack the cross-report consistency expected if experiencers were observing the same external spiritual realm.
moves.inventoryRationale: Concise empirical objection to a common separability claim.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: differs significantly depending on that person's religious perspective
electronically stimulates the brain
intelligent presence is in the room
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.
moves.proposition: Near-death descriptions vary with prior religion, while direct brain stimulation can induce sensed presences and out-of-body impressions, favoring culturally interpreted brain events over soul travel.
moves.inventoryRationale: Joins the cultural-variation and induced-experience evidence into a single source-contiguous empirical inference.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: whatever they expected to see
never a revelation of spirituality
illusions that only accentuate preconceived notions
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.
moves.proposition: Near-death visions reproduce subjects' prior religious expectations rather than revealing unfamiliar common facts, indicating internally generated illusions rather than encounters by a separable soul.
moves.inventoryRationale: Distinct predictive argument from expectation-dependence.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: built a network of synaptic connections
everything you know or remember
dependent on that cerebral mesh
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.
moves.proposition: Learning and memory are embodied in acquired synaptic networks, and their impairment or rebuilding after stroke shows that a person's cognitive continuity depends on that physical organization.
moves.inventoryRationale: Connects memory and identity to persisting brain organization rather than to unchanged matter or a separate subject.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the mind is an emergent aspect of the body
your mind is not just data
you wouldn't be you anymore
moves.attributionBasis: Clear negative opening.

responseComponents.component: Treats personhood as an emergent property of the integrated whole brain and body rather than an indivisible extra entity.
Argues that identity depends on organized neural, bodily, experiential, and endocrine continuity, not on numerical sameness of material particles.

moves.proposition: The mind emerges from the integrated brain and body; transferring information into a differently organized body would alter skills, preferences, emotions, and identity because the person is embodied organization, not detachable data.
moves.inventoryRationale: The negative's main account of embodied personhood and persistence.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: make you literally a different person
at what point does he changed
literally a different person than when he was five
moves.attributionBasis: Hernandez's rebuttal after the moderator's handoff.

responseComponents.component: Presses whether changes in beliefs, memories, and bodily organization literally replace the person, and requests a principled threshold for such replacement.

moves.proposition: If bodily or psychological change makes a numerically different person, the embodied account must explain when yesterday's or childhood person ceased to exist rather than merely developed.
moves.inventoryRationale: Major direct objection to Aron Ra's embodied-identity account.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: all I did was give data
consciousness as the ebb and flow of neurons
the mind really does emanate from and is generated by the brain
moves.attributionBasis: Aron Ra's rebuttal after an explicit handoff.

responseComponents.component: Counters the conceptual separation by citing a generated-neural account of consciousness.
Maintains that conscious experience emanates from neural activity rather than requiring a separate bearer.

moves.proposition: Neural evidence and the cited emergent account support consciousness as generated by the activity of a healthy brain rather than by an immaterial subject.
moves.inventoryRationale: Direct negative reply to the affirmative's mental-property arguments, though it asserts generation more than it explains intentional content.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: all data is going to be inconclusive
immaterial substance which is a contradiction
there would be a way to verify
moves.attributionBasis: Clear continuation of Aron Ra's rebuttal.

responseComponents.component: Rejects insulating the proposed entity from verification by labeling the question metaphysical.
Objects that empirical inconclusiveness was imposed by definition rather than established.
Challenges 'immaterial substance' as incoherent and insufficiently defined.

moves.proposition: Calling all evidence inconclusive by definition evades testing, and 'immaterial substance' remains incoherent unless Hernandez states verifiable implications of the entity.
moves.inventoryRationale: Major definitional and burden challenge repeated throughout cross-examination.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I'm not sure about freewill myself
I don't think that I necessarily do
you can't have free will
moves.attributionBasis: Clear continuation of Aron Ra's rebuttal; the subsequent biblical extension is excluded.

responseComponents.component: Declines to concede libertarian free will and therefore rejects it as an established premise requiring a soul.
Questions the move from practical responsibility to a metaphysical faculty whose existence remains disputed.

moves.proposition: Aron Ra is uncertain that libertarian free will exists, so Hernandez cannot use its mere assumption as evidence for a soul.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important concession of uncertainty coupled with a direct premise-level objection.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it's perceived damage
I'm not a neurologist
the signal is received and interpreted as pain
moves.attributionBasis: Aron Ra answers Hernandez during cross-examination; speaker identity is clear from the alternating questions and answers.

responseComponents.component: Identifies pain with the physically mediated perception and interpretation of damage, while conceding inability to provide the detailed neural mechanism.

moves.proposition: Pain is the sensory reception and interpretation of bodily damage and is physical, although Aron Ra concedes he cannot specify the detailed neural mechanism.
moves.inventoryRationale: Substantive answer to the qualia challenge, retaining the important explanatory limitation.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I can change my mind when given evidence
based on your past experiences
doesn't mean that I own strain prohibited
moves.attributionBasis: Clear answer by Aron Ra during Hernandez's cross-examination.

responseComponents.component: Argues that causal influence by history and character does not prevent evidence-responsive decision-making.
Denies that rational revision requires an uncaused chooser or immaterial source.

moves.proposition: Decisions are strongly shaped by experience and character, yet a person can still revise beliefs in response to evidence; rationality need not mean exemption from causal influence.
moves.inventoryRationale: The clearest negative account separating reasons-responsiveness from libertarian origination.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: that's a complete non sequitur
physical ism is a view
purely physical properties and parts
moves.attributionBasis: Cross-examination exchange with clear content and alternating speakers.

responseComponents.component: Rejects the inference from differences in bodily quantity to degrees of personhood, treating value and personhood as classifications not measured by mass.

moves.proposition: It does not follow from physicalism that a larger body is more of a person or more valuable, because personhood is not defined as bodily mass.
moves.inventoryRationale: Direct rebuttal to the affirmative's personhood-by-degrees extension.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there would be certain things we would expect
damage the brain and change how it thinks
how did we stop the thinking
moves.attributionBasis: Aron Ra's questioning is identifiable from content and Hernandez's immediate instrument reply.

responseComponents.component: Challenges the instrument analogy by noting that damage changes or stops the very thinking attributed to the soul.
Asks what the soul adds when cognitive capacities track physical integrity.

moves.proposition: If an immaterial thinker rather than the brain performs cognition, it is unexplained why damaging the brain changes or stops the thinking itself.
moves.inventoryRationale: Sharp diagnostic objection to the dependence-versus-identity defense.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the soul being immortal
there is a cause and effect
I can damage a guitar and a piano
moves.attributionBasis: Hernandez's answer is explicit after Aron Ra's question.

responseComponents.component: Clarifies that the debate case did not assume immortality or complete independence from embodiment.
Maintains that damage to the bodily instrument can impair expression or access without damaging the nonphysical content or subject.

moves.proposition: The case does not require the embodied soul to be wholly independent or presently immortal; injury can damage the instrument it uses and thereby impair cognitive operation without establishing identity.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important qualification preventing the negative from attacking a stronger separability claim than Hernandez defended.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: when you in the brain and stroke
the split brain thing
why would that f soul would not have that dysfunction
moves.attributionBasis: Content and the ensuing Hernandez response identify Aron Ra, but captions are heavily garbled within the span.

responseComponents.component: Adds split-brain and stroke deficits as cases where cognition fragments along physical neural divisions, demanding an account of why a unitary soul shares the dysfunction.

moves.proposition: Stroke and split-brain deficits track particular neural divisions, which is difficult to reconcile with a unitary soul that supposedly performs the undivided perceiving and thinking.
moves.inventoryRationale: Source-required split-brain challenge and a distinct refinement of generic brain dependence.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: looking for the reason
inconsistent with that
unicellular organisms without any neurons
moves.attributionBasis: Clear question and explanation by Aron Ra during cross-examination.

responseComponents.component: Demands a positive reason for the additional component and argues that memory-like and reasoning behavior in neuronless organisms undercuts its claimed necessity.

moves.proposition: Since physical organisms display relevant capacities even without neurons, Hernandez must positively show what additional explanatory work the proposed soul performs.
moves.inventoryRationale: Central burden-of-proof challenge tied to biological examples rather than a bare demand.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: exhibit signs of consciousness
consciousness itself is an emergent aspect
there are degrees of it
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Aron Ra answer in cross-examination.

responseComponents.component: Offers behavioral evidence and graded emergence as the basis for attributing consciousness without positing an indivisible private substance.

moves.proposition: Other consciousness is inferred from observable signs, and consciousness occurs in degrees as an emergent capacity rather than appearing as an all-or-nothing immaterial property.
moves.inventoryRationale: Supplies Aron Ra's positive epistemic and emergent account of consciousness.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: physical objects aggregates
I am the same person
still 100 percent a person
moves.attributionBasis: Clear affirmative closing statement.

responseComponents.component: Argues that changing memories or physical parts does not erase numerical personal identity.
Contrasts persisting personhood with the replacement of material components and bodily capacities.
Restates personhood as an all-or-nothing status not grounded in quantitative physical features.

moves.proposition: Loss or gain of memories, parts, or bodily abilities does not make Hernandez less of a person or someone else, so personal identity is not grounded solely in brain and body.
moves.inventoryRationale: Closing synthesis of the affirmative persistence argument after the negative objections.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: definition of personhood
not weight and measured in a gradient
makes so many unwarranted assumptions
moves.attributionBasis: Aron Ra's closing begins immediately after Hernandez's closing and moderator handoff.

responseComponents.component: Denies that physicalism measures personhood by quantities such as height or weight.
Argues that persistent person-status can be definitional and does not demonstrate an extra substance.

moves.proposition: The affirmative's degree argument assumes without justification that physical personhood must be measured by bodily weight or size; physicalism need not make that identification.
moves.inventoryRationale: Concise closing rebuttal to the indivisibility and equal-personhood inference.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the evidence they most like to present
people are actually leaving their body
the god helmet that duplicates all of these effects
moves.attributionBasis: Substantive answer to the moderator's question about Aron Ra's strongest argument.
moves.proposition: The strongest popular case for separability relies on out-of-body reports, but competing studies and brain-stimulation replication undermine the inference that subjects literally leave their bodies.
moves.inventoryRationale: Late direct statement of the negative's strongest empirical objection, answering the moderator substantively.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I think they actually do happen
a lot of verified in des
something I haven't studied to the satisfaction
moves.attributionBasis: Hernandez's substantive answer to the moderator's question about whether his case relied on near-death experiences.

responseComponents.component: Claims that some near-death cases are verified rather than merely inconsistent anecdotes.
Denies that induced experiences exhaust the evidential category.
Maintains that some reports allegedly contain knowledge not explained by prior expectation.
Concedes he has not studied the material enough to make it part of his primary defended case.

moves.proposition: Hernandez believes some near-death reports are verified and evidential, but concedes he has not studied them sufficiently to present or defend them as a main argument here.
moves.inventoryRationale: Important limited concession preserving both his late empirical claim and its admitted evidential status.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: verified signed off by doctors
doesn't mean beaches don't exist
just because you can replicate an experience
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Hernandez response in the audience-question exchange.

responseComponents.component: Argues that artificially producing a type of experience does not prove that every naturally occurring instance lacks an external object.
Challenges the inference from neurological replication to universal falsity of reported out-of-body events.

moves.proposition: Replicating an experience through brain stimulation does not by itself show that all experiences of that type are unreal, just as simulating a beach experience would not show beaches do not exist.
moves.inventoryRationale: Major direct rebuttal to the God-helmet replication argument.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the god helmet isn't doing squat to their soul
entirely physical
we have proofs that they are
moves.attributionBasis: Aron Ra's immediate response is clear from content and alternation.

responseComponents.component: Argues that a physical device producing specific false perceptions is positive evidence that the relevant experiences arise through physical brain processes.

moves.proposition: A physical device can generate false sensed presences and out-of-body impressions through brain stimulation, so those experiences demonstrate physical susceptibility rather than independent soul perception.
moves.inventoryRationale: Direct negative response to the simulation analogy.

moves.speaker: Eric Hernandez
quoteEligibleExactSpans: incorrigibility of your mental states
I was not incorrect about my mental states
they're not identical
moves.attributionBasis: Clear Hernandez answer during the God-helmet exchange.

responseComponents.component: Distinguishes the occurrence and character of an experience from the physical object or cause being represented.
Argues that stimulation may make the external judgment false while leaving the subject infallibly aware that the conscious experience itself occurs.

moves.proposition: A subject can be wrong about the external object of an experience but not about presently having that experience; this incorrigibility distinguishes mental states from physical objects.
moves.inventoryRationale: Late development of the affirmative property-difference case prompted by hallucination evidence.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I don't trust things
testing these against my own experience
what fact would stand against this
moves.attributionBasis: Clear substantive answer to an audience question.

responseComponents.component: Explains reliability through graded confidence, intersubjective checking, data, and attempted falsification rather than through an uncaused soul.

moves.proposition: Belief reliability comes in degrees and is improved by checking impressions against experience, other observers, data, and tests designed to prove a claim wrong.
moves.inventoryRationale: The negative's most developed positive account of rational warrant.

moves.speaker: Aron Ra
quoteEligibleExactSpans: all my decisions are not determined
I can still make a decision based on information
before I even know what it is
moves.attributionBasis: Clear continuation of Aron Ra's answer.

responseComponents.component: Rejects the claim that causal history fixes a decision before the relevant evidence is encountered.
Maintains that information-responsive choice can ground rational accountability without a soul.

moves.proposition: Past tendencies influence but do not predetermine acceptance or rejection of evidence before it is encountered; decisions remain responsive to new information.
moves.inventoryRationale: Records Aron Ra's own compatibilist-leaning qualification rather than recasting him as endorsing strict determinism.

selectionRationale: The inventory selects 42 chronologically ordered, independently assessable moves across six source-required clusters. It preserves Hernandez's philosophical case, Aron Ra's biological and empirical case, the distinction between dependence evidence and deductive identity, the gap between criticizing reductive physicalism and positively demonstrating a soul, and explicit concessions about brain effects, free-will uncertainty, neurological expertise, and the limited role of near-death evidence. Moderator material, personal invective, extended theology, and repeated summaries were excluded unless a substantive answer directly bore on the soul motion.
